properties.name: Corporate Core
properties.known_for: Arcologies, luxury towers, and curated civic space
properties.description: The pristine Seattle shown on corporate feeds: towers, luxury arcologies, corporate hotels, immaculate public spaces, security drones, and the surviving institutions of civic government.

properties.name: Queen Anne
properties.known_for: Compounds, boutique arcologies, and the Space Needle
properties.description: Historic houses have become executive compounds and boutique arcologies. The hill is easy to defend, and this is where wealthy Seattle tells itself that civilization survived.

properties.name: Helios Corridor
properties.description: A dense biomedical research corridor dominated by the five-building Helios campus and its elevated central platform. Its skyline has become inseparable from stories of Aurum Rex.

properties.name: Meridian
properties.known_for: Night markets, clubs, fixers, and street clinics
properties.access: Open streets with uneven municipal control
properties.description: Counterculture survives here as night markets, independent clubs, street clinics, runners, activists, and businesses serving people who prefer not to appear in corporate records. Its exact identity is still being defined.

properties.name: Old City
properties.access: Active by day; selectively lawless after dark
properties.description: Pre-Razz buildings, alleys, and surviving underground spaces support legitimate commerce by day and runners, smugglers, unlicensed cyberware, and information markets after dark.

properties.name: Ballard Reach
properties.known_for: Repair yards, fisheries, smugglers, and Currentborn
properties.access: Water routes and guarded industrial roads
properties.description: Boat repair, fisheries, small shipyards, smugglers, and Currentborn communities give Ballard enough maritime capacity to maintain unusual independence from the corporate core.

properties.name: Fremont Works
properties.known_for: Riggers, salvage engineers, art, and workshops
properties.access: Independent streets north of the canal
properties.description: Small workshops, Riggers, salvage engineers, artists, and eccentric institutions turned the neighborhood's cultivated weirdness into practical resistance to corporate homogenization.

properties.name: University Enclave
properties.known_for: Research, sealed laboratories, and controlled knowledge
properties.access: Public campus edges; restricted research interior
properties.description: The University of Washington still looks enough like a university to use the name, but corporate priorities control its research and intellectual property. Sealed pre-Razz laboratories remain beneath it.

properties.name: Working Seattle
properties.known_for: Dense communities and the labor that keeps Seattle alive
properties.description: Mixed communities of immigrants, metahumans, municipal workers, and families keep the city functioning without receiving corporate-core investment. Social cohesion is strong; infrastructure is not.

properties.name: Bombshell
properties.known_for: War ruins, warehouses, rail yards, and exclusion blocks
properties.access: Usable corridors separated by sealed ruins
properties.description: The industrial south still bears the physical scars of the Black Helix–Dominion war. Functional warehouses and rail lines stand beside shattered exclusion zones and the fortified Boeing Field complex.

properties.name: West Seattle
properties.description: The loss and degradation of bridge infrastructure made West Seattle almost a separate town. Neighborhood associations and local defense groups carry more practical authority than City Hall.
